context.discussion_purpose: Define an ABM playbook that explains the entire process from identifying accounts to closing deals, with optional supporting tools per step.
objectives: Explain the full ABM process from identifying accounts to closing deals.
Define six numbered steps: TAM and stakeholder mapping; AI account research and enrichment; track the signals; Score + Tier Accounts; CRM components; demand generation.
List supporting technology options per step without implying a mandatory software stack.
Show unnumbered downstream activities (Slack notification, enroll in sequences, CRM tasks) leading to the closed-won outcome.
existing_systems: A GTM framework discussed previously (referenced for comparison only).
independent_subjects: Personal logistics (weekend, lunch, invoice, delivery, car service) — excluded.
material_limitations: Speaker identities and roles are not named.
Vendors for signal categories, and tools for several demand-generation activities, are explicitly not finalized.
Numerical scoring thresholds and an awareness-to-tier mapping are explicitly undefined.
context.discussion_order_note: Steps were discussed out of order (6 before 4 and 5); the recap (segment-205 to segment-219) is the authoritative sequence.
context.summary: Two speakers define a six-step ABM playbook, the tools that can optionally support each step, a three-way signal taxonomy, awareness stages and account tiers, a one-to-one / one-to-many demand-generation split, and downstream activities ending at closed-won. Multiple corrections and exclusions are stated explicitly.

topics.name: Our 6-Step ABM Playbook
topics.explanation: Overall ABM playbook from identifying accounts to closing deals; six numbered steps plus downstream activities.

topics.name: Tool optionality policy
topics.explanation: Tools are alternatives / supporting technology options, not a mandatory stack; may repeat across steps; unfinalized names are not invented.

topics.name: Step 1 — TAM and stakeholder mapping
topics.explanation: Identify the total addressable market and relevant stakeholders within target accounts; eight supporting options.

topics.name: Step 2 — AI account research and enrichment
topics.explanation: AI-assisted research and enrichment of accounts; ten supporting tools.

topics.name: Step 3 — Track the signals
topics.explanation: Track buying signals, engagement signals and account activity, categorized as first-, second- and third-party.

topics.name: Step 4 — Score + Tier Accounts
topics.explanation: Five awareness stages and three account tiers; no numeric thresholds and no fixed mapping between them.

topics.name: Step 5 — CRM components
topics.explanation: HubSpot or Salesforce; CRM records informed by steps 1–4 and supporting demand generation.

topics.name: Step 6 — Demand generation
topics.explanation: Demand generation organized as one-to-one and one-to-many (not inbound/outbound).

topics.name: Downstream activities and final outcome
topics.explanation: Unnumbered follow-up after demand generation: Slack notification, enroll in sequences, CRM tasks, then closed-won.

facts.statement: The playbook has six numbered steps; downstream activities are not step seven.
The ABM playbook is similar to the previously discussed GTM framework but is specifically ABM.
Step 1 has eight supporting options: Sales Navigator, AI Ark, Clay, Findymail, Ocean.io, DiscoLike, Landbase, custom scrapers.
Step 2 has ten tools: Ocean.io, Claygent, Sumble, Codex, Tavily, Freckle, Claude Code, Findymail, BetterContact, AI Ark.
Tavily is used for web research.
Step 3 is described as probably the most detailed step.
Signals tracked include buying signals, engagement signals and account activity.
There are eleven third-party signal categories.
There are eight first-party signal categories.
There are six second-party signal categories.
Gated content means things like downloadable resources behind a form.
Warm introductions are tracked as a second-party signal and are also a one-to-one demand-generation activity (same concept, different context).
There are five awareness stages in order: identified, aware, interested, considering, selecting.
There are three account tiers: Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3.
Awareness stages and account tiering are related concepts with no defined fixed mapping.
Either HubSpot or Salesforce can be used for CRM depending on the existing technology stack; both are not required.
Account mapping, research, tracked signals and scoring information inform the CRM records.
The CRM supports demand generation and connects account intelligence and prioritization with demand-generation activities.
Demand generation has four one-to-one activities and eight one-to-many activities.
Personalized video could technically be one-to-one, but video outreach is classified as one-to-many in this playbook.
Downstream order: Slack notification, enroll in sequences, CRM tasks, then closed-won as the final outcome.
Some tools appear in multiple sections because they have different purposes in different stages.
Tools are supporting technology options; the playbook does not recommend every company use all of them.

activities.name: TAM and stakeholder mapping
activities.description: Identify the total addressable market and the relevant stakeholders within target accounts.
activities.sequence_note: Step 1 of 6 (recap).

activities.name: AI account research and enrichment
activities.description: Research and enrich target accounts with AI-assisted tools.
activities.sequence_note: Step 2 of 6 (recap).

activities.name: Track the signals
activities.description: Track buying signals, engagement signals and account activity across first-party (8), second-party (6) and third-party (11) categories. Vendors per category are not finalized and must not be guessed.
activities.sequence_note: Step 3 of 6 (recap).

activities.name: Score + Tier Accounts
activities.description: Assess accounts across five awareness stages (identified, aware, interested, considering, selecting) and assign Tier 1, Tier 2 or Tier 3. No numerical thresholds; no fixed stage-to-tier mapping.
activities.sequence_note: Step 4 of 6 (recap); discussed after Step 6.

activities.name: CRM components
activities.description: Maintain CRM records in HubSpot or Salesforce (either, depending on the existing stack), informed by account mapping, research, tracked signals and scoring; connects account intelligence and prioritization with demand generation.
activities.purpose: System of record linking intelligence and prioritization to demand generation.
activities.sequence_note: Step 5 of 6 (recap).

activities.name: Demand generation
activities.description: Run demand generation in two groups — one-to-one (4 activities) and one-to-many (8 activities); explicitly not organized as inbound/outbound.
activities.sequence_note: Step 6 of 6 (recap); discussed before Steps 4 and 5.

decisions.statement: Name the deliverable "Our 6-Step ABM Playbook".
Tools are alternatives / supporting technology options, not a mandatory software stack.
Proposal: use Apollo for TAM and stakeholder mapping.
Do not include Apollo in this playbook.
Step 1 options: Sales Navigator, AI Ark, Clay, Findymail, Ocean.io, DiscoLike, Landbase, custom scrapers.
Use Claygent (not Clay) in Step 2.
Speaker 2's note "Claude" for Step 2.
Correction: specifically Claude Code, not Claude, in Step 2.
Tools may appear in multiple sections; keep Ocean.io in Step 2 even though it is in Step 1.
Divide signals into first-party, second-party and third-party categories.
Website visits belong to first-party signals, not third-party.
Email opens are not a separate first-party category for now.
Warm intros are both a second-party signal and a one-to-one demand-generation activity.
Do not specify or guess vendors for signal categories; preserve the categories.
Proposal: organize demand generation as inbound and outbound.
Organize demand generation as one-to-one and one-to-many.
Video outreach is classified under one-to-many for this playbook.
Ad platforms: LinkedIn, Meta and Google.
No Reddit ads in this version.
Social content platforms: YouTube, LinkedIn and X (formerly Twitter).
Webflow for on-site content; LinkedIn for connection requests; Gmail for warm intros; HubSpot for manual outreach.
Keep parallel dialing and gifting campaigns; finalize their tools later.
Name Step 4 "Score + Tier Accounts".
Proposal: 0–100 scoring model / 80–100 for Tier 1.
No numerical scoring thresholds; do not include proposed numbers.
Initial awareness order: identified, aware, interested, selecting, considering.
Corrected awareness order: identified, aware, interested, considering, selecting.
Proposal: map identified to Tier 3 and selecting to Tier 1.
No fixed mapping between awareness stages and tiers.
Proposal: HubSpot, Salesforce and Pipedrive as CRMs.
CRM: HubSpot and Salesforce only (either/or); exclude Pipedrive for this version.
Downstream activities are not step seven; the playbook keeps six numbered steps.
Speaker 2's proposed order: Slack notification then CRM tasks.
Sequence enrollment comes before CRM tasks.
No closed-lost branch in this version; show the path toward closed-won.

requirements.statement: Explain the entire process from identifying accounts to closing deals.
Do not suggest that everyone needs to buy every tool; present tools as options.
Allow the same tool in multiple sections; do not deduplicate across steps.
Preserve all signal categories and do not guess missing vendor names.
Do not remove demand-generation activities whose supporting tools are unconfirmed.
Do not include numerical scoring thresholds.
Do not invent a mapping between awareness stages and tiers.
Account mapping, research, tracked signals and scoring information should inform CRM records.
Keep six numbered steps; show downstream activities and closed-won as unnumbered.
Illustrate only the path toward closed-won (no closed-lost branch).
Do not invent names for tools that have not been finalized.
Do not organize demand generation as inbound/outbound.
